title: Majestic Style
summary: Use a pinned rook sacrifice to promote with check, then compare a direct mate with a carefully controlled queen promotion.

nodes.question: How can White improve the timing of promotion?
nodes.explanation: The rook on g2 sits behind the pawn. Rh2 can pin that rook against its king on a2 and redirect it before promotion.

nodes.question: Stop promotion or allow it deliberately?
nodes.explanation: With the king on d3, White can either mate before promotion or move to c3 and keep mating threats after ...a1=Q+.

branches.title: Deflect the rook and finish before promotion
commentary: Begin after ...Rg2. Earlier king retreat maneuvers remain source context; this six-piece position is checked exactly.
Rh2 pins the black rook on the second rank against Ka2. It threatens to remove the defender of the g-pawn.
Rxh2 accepts the rook offer and leaves the g-file. This is the source’s selected response.
g8=Q+ promotes with check along the diagonal to a2. With the black rook diverted to h2, it can no longer capture the new queen.
Kb2 chooses the illustrated outward king route. The other king replies are outside this selected branch.
Qb8+ checks the king and attacks Rh2 along b8-c7-d6-e5-f4-g3-h2.
Ka1 retreats to the corner and leaves the rook available to capture.
Qxh2 removes the rook. White must still deal with the a-pawn.
a2 brings the pawn one step from promotion.
Kd3 approaches the corner, controlling c2 and c3.
Kb1 is the only legal king move; the pawn on a2 is blocked by the king while it stands on a1.
Qc2+ checks b1 with the queen protected by Kd3.
Ka1 is forced back into the corner.
Qc1# checks along the first rank. Kd3 protects c2, the queen covers b1 and b2, and Black’s own pawn occupies a2.
branches.explanation: Qc1# checks along the first rank. Kd3 protects c2, the queen covers b1 and b2, and Black’s own pawn occupies a2.

branches.title: Allow a queen, then restrict its checks
commentary: This is the source’s stylish alternative after Kd3 Kb1, not a jump directly from the earlier king on e3.
Kc3 deliberately allows promotion, preparing to approach on b3.
a1=Q+ promotes with check along the diagonal a1-b2-c3.
Kb3 steps off the diagonal. Qh2 covers a2 and b2; the nearby queen checks on a3, a4 or c3 would let the white king capture the checking queen.
Qa5 is the illustrated queen reply. It does not check Kb3 or stop White’s contact mate.
Qb2# is protected by Kb3. The black queen on a5 cannot capture b2 or interpose against a queen checking the adjacent king on b1.
branches.explanation: Qb2# is protected by Kb3. The black queen on a5 cannot capture b2 or interpose against a queen checking the adjacent king on b1.

branches.title: If Black moves the king after promoting
commentary: Compare the other illustrated reply after the same deliberate promotion.
Kc3 prepares the king’s b3 approach while allowing Black to promote.
a1=Q+ checks along the diagonal.
Kb3 leaves White threatening a protected contact queen mate.
Kc1 is the illustrated king reply, leaving the queen on a1.
Qc2# is protected by Kb3 and checks c1. The queen covers the remaining flights on b1, d1, b2 and d2; Black’s queen cannot block an adjacent-file check.
branches.explanation: Qc2# is protected by Kb3 and checks c1. The queen covers the remaining flights on b1, d1, b2 and d2; Black’s queen cannot block an adjacent-file check.

branches.title: Promote before redirecting the rook
commentary: Before sacrificing the rook on h2, compare immediate promotion.
g8=Q+ checks along the diagonal to a2, but gives up the forced win because the rook on g2 can capture the new queen.
Rxg8 removes the new queen along the g-file.
Rxg8 recaptures, but White’s king on e3 is still too far from the a-pawn and its king. The exact remaining rook ending is drawn.
branches.explanation: Rxg8 recaptures, but White’s king on e3 is still too far from the a-pawn and its king. The exact remaining rook ending is drawn.

exercises.prompt: Why sacrifice the rook before promoting?
exercises.answer: ...Rxh2 removes the rook from the g-file. White then promotes with check, gaining time to fork the king and rook.

exercises.prompt: Why is Kc3 different from simply ignoring the passer?
exercises.answer: The king plans Kb3 after the checking promotion. Its own queen covers checking routes and supports contact mate; the displayed continuations are checked individually.

startContext: Begin after ...Rg2 at 95 seconds. Earlier rook checks and king retreat are source context. The sacrifice, one promotion-check king route, direct mate, two illustrated queen-ending replies and drawing immediate promotion are checked here; no exhaustive proof tree is displayed.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
